caption: What if gravity doubled for a day? You wake up and your 60 kg body reads 120 kg on the scale, because weight is just mass times gravity. Under extra g, blood gets pulled from your head toward your legs, so standing up fast could leave you dizzy. Your best jump reaches only half as high: same push, double the pull. A dropped phone hits the floor about 40% faster, since impact speed grows with the square root of gravity. A cricket hit that flew 80 metres would land roughly half as far, and ocean waves of the same size would race about 40% faster. Could you survive? Relaxed, unprotected people tolerate about 3.5 g, and fighter pilots in g-suits handle around 9 g, so a 2 g day would be survivable but exhausting. Plot twist: you may have felt more already. A typical roller coaster can push you to about 3.5 g, just for a few seconds. Could YOU last a full 2 g day? 👇
